text.p: Russia launched a satellite on Thursday to improve its telephone and television network, a space official said.

A heavy Proton-K booster rocket with the Express telecommunications satellite blasted off from the Baikonur cosmodrome in Kazakhstan at 9.51 p.m Moscow time (1751 GMT), said a spokesman for the Military Space Forces' headquarters.
"The launch was made after ground specialists replaced a defective part of the booster," the spokesman told Reuters, adding that the satellite should reach its orbit eight hours after launch.
The launch was postponed for 24 hours because of the fault in the Proton-K rocket.
Russia plans to launch several Express satellites over the next few months to replace 12 outdated Gorizont satellites which have been providing its television coverage.
The first Express satellite was launched in 1994 and has been used to transmit Russian television programmes as well as programmes from Portugal and France.
Earlier this month, a Proton booster successfully launched a U.S.-built satellite for the international telecommunications organisation Inmarsat.
